Welcome

I'm glad you're here.

This takes about eight minutes. It covers what to expect, how sessions work, how money and cancelling work, and how to reach me. You can stop and come back any time.

A little about me. I'm a licensed clinical social worker. I work with trauma, burnout and the kind of tired that comes from holding it together for everyone else. I use a lot of metaphors and some humor, and I explain what I'm doing and why. I'm neurodivergent myself, so I know some of this from the inside.

What happens, in order

  1. Forms. You'll finish a short set of forms in your secure client portal. They take about 15 minutes, and you can save and come back.
  2. This slide show. The part you're in now.

  4. After that. We find a rhythm that works for your life.

3 of 13

How I work

Talking helps, and some things live in the body where words don't reach. I'm trained in EMDR and the Flash Technique, and I use parts work and body-based practices alongside conversation. The point is to include your nervous system, not only your thoughts.

  • You set the pace. You can say "slower," "skip that" or "not today" at any point.
  • You won't have to retell your whole story to start.
  • Most sessions end with one small practice, five minutes or less, to try on your own.

I'm trained in these methods, not certified in them. I'll tell you what I'm using and why.

4 of 13

Sessions by video

All my sessions are by secure video, through your client portal. A few practical things:

  • You must be in California during every session. I'm licensed in California, and that's where the law lets me work with you. Traveling? Tell me ahead of time.
  • Find a private spot. Headphones help a lot if anyone might overhear.
  • Use a device with a camera and microphone, and a steady connection.
  • If the connection drops, I'll try to reconnect for a few minutes. If that doesn't work, I'll call the number you gave me, so keep your phone nearby.

5 of 13

Your first session

We start with a few practical questions: where you are, a phone number, and an emergency contact. Then we talk about what brought you here.

  • You decide how much to share. There's no test and no wrong answer.
  • I'll ask about what you want to be different, and what you've already tried.
  • At the end, I'll tell you honestly how I'd work with you and what a good next few weeks could look like. If I don't think I'm the right fit, I'll say so and help you find someone who is.

6 of 13

Privacy, and where it stops

What you tell me stays between us. There are a few exceptions the law requires, and I'll go over them in your forms.

  • If someone is in serious danger, including you.
  • If a child, an older adult or a dependent adult is being harmed.
  • If a court orders records.

Text and email aren't fully secure, since your phone company or anyone with your phone could see them. They're fine for scheduling and short check-ins. Keep the details of what you're working through for our sessions or the client portal.

7 of 13

If things get hard between sessions

Hard stretches happen, and they're a normal part of this work. Here's what to do.

  • Use the small practice from our session, and write down what you notice so we can talk about it.
  • Message me in the portal. I reply within one business day. I'm not an emergency service, and I don't watch messages for emergencies.
  • If you might hurt yourself, or you're in crisis, call or text 988. In an emergency, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.

We'll make a simple safety plan together early on. Everyone gets one. It isn't a sign anything is wrong.

8 of 13

How insurance works with me

I'm not in network with any insurance plan. That means you pay me directly, and you can ask your plan to reimburse you. This is called "out of network."

  • You pay my fee: $175 for 50 minutes, $200 for 60 minutes. Couples sessions are $225.
  • I keep a card on file and charge it after each session.
  • I give you a statement ("superbill") with the codes your plan needs. You submit it to your insurer.
  • Before we start, I'll send you a written Good Faith Estimate of your costs.

Whether, and how much, your plan reimburses depends on your plan. I can't promise it will.

9 of 13

Questions to ask your insurance

A short call can save you surprises. Ask your plan:

  • Do I have out-of-network mental health benefits?
  • What is my out-of-network deductible, and how much have I met?
  • What percent of the cost do you reimburse after that?
  • Is video therapy covered?
  • Do I need approval from the plan before I start?
  • How do I submit a claim, and how long does it take?

Tell them the session codes are 90837, 90834 and 90791. Write down the date, who you talked to, and what they said.

10 of 13

Cancelling or rescheduling

Please tell me by 3:00 PM the day before your session if you need to cancel or change it. That gives me time to offer the slot to someone else.

If you cancel after that, or miss the session, the full session fee applies. Insurance doesn't reimburse missed sessions. If something truly out of your control happens, tell me. I'd rather hear it and talk it through with you.

About AI note-taking

I may use an AI tool inside my records system to help write my session notes. It's optional. I'll ask you separately, in writing.

  • If you say yes, the tool turns the conversation into a draft that I read, correct and finish myself.
  • If you say no, nothing changes about your care. I write my own notes.
  • You can change your mind later.

The consent form explains exactly how it works. Read it before you sign.
